lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "For every idea I could make a video of, find which of the formats in my library suit it best, and record the best few per idea with why", and give it step.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:rank-library-formats-against-concepts and its input (the worked example shows one).
3. Read what comes back: Two steps.
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: record:setting (records:read).

worked_examples.title: Match every video format I have collected to every idea I could film, and keep the best fits on its own sample
worked_examples.ask: For every idea I could make a video of, find which of the formats in my library suit it best, and record the best few per idea with why
worked_examples.given: The input {"step":"catalog","library":"library","concepts":{"files":["ideas/A.md"]},"settings_record":"record:setting:rank-library-formats-against-concepts~film~sample-film"}, with 1 example row (record:setting) already kept.
worked_examples.hands_back: It answered {"step":"catalog","candidates":2,"concepts":1,"settings_from":{"id":"record:setting:rank-library-formats-against-concepts~film~sample-film","from":"made up for this sample"}}.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
